per_option_rationale.rationale: When expanding -3(x-1), the student writes -3x - 3 instead of -3x + 3, dropping the sign on the constant term: 4x+10-3x-3 = 24 gives x + 7 = 24, x = 17.
The student correctly reaches x + 13 = 24 but then computes 24 - 13 = 12 instead of 11, a one-unit arithmetic slip in the final subtraction.

When multiplying through by 6, the student distributes 2 to 2x but not to the constant 5, writing 2(2x+5) as 4x+5 instead of 4x+10. This is an order-of-operations error: multiplication is not applied to all terms in the bracket. The equation becomes 4x+5-3x+3 = 24, giving x + 8 = 24, x = 16.

explanation: Multiply every term by LCM(3,2) = 6: 2(2x+5) - 3(x-1) = 24. Expand carefully: 4x+10-3x+3 = 24. Collect: x + 13 = 24. Solve: x = 11.

explanation_sections.punchline: The answer is x = 11. The key step is expanding -3(x-1) as -3x + 3, not -3x - 3. A sign error on this term shifts the answer to 17.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the LCM of all denominators and multiply every term through by it to clear fractions first. Then expand each bracket, paying attention to signs. Collect all x-terms on one side and constants on the other.
explanation_sections.lesson: When multiplying a bracket with a negative sign outside, every term inside changes sign. -3(x-1) = -3x + 3, never -3x - 3. Write the expansion step explicitly rather than doing it mentally.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 seconds. Finding LCM and multiplying through takes about 20 seconds. Expansion and collection of terms takes about 30 seconds. Verify by substituting x = 11 back: (27/3) - (10/2) = 9 - 5 = 4. This check takes under 15 seconds.
